answer: Read graders like tracks in tundra snow. On contested answers only (where an independent panel splits), identities whose scores move in lockstep across many seats get their grading weight pooled into one vote; a farm grading from one script leaves a spiral of matching prints, like wind ripples on a dune. Evasion: add random noise to each fake's grades, which drags down their accuracy pay. Wrongly hit: honest experts who agree because they're right, so easy seats are excluded, pooling is gradual, nothing is slashed, and the threshold (an assumption) is public.
